extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal by systematically traversing a website's subpages to extract high-quality data. It evaluates the capacity of LLMs to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically, focusing on text-based reasoning abilities using a Question-Answer format. The benchmark includes 680 queries from four real-world scenarios across over 1373 webpages, covering domains such as education, conference, organization, and game, with both single-source and multi-source QA types.
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.citeAs: WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves a two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. In the first stage, GPT-4o performs initial annotations by traversing official websites recursively to collect information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages. Queries are constructed based on the provided page information, focusing on either a single page or multiple pages simultaneously. Queries are verified and filtered to retain only legitimate QA pairs with short answers containing entities. In the second stage, crowd-sourced human annotators rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers to ensure correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites from conference, organization, education, and game domains were used as the raw data source. The root pages were identified through Google searches using keywords such as 'conference official website' or 'game official website,' followed by manual filtering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The collected data underwent preprocessing to filter out incomplete entries and ensure the QA pairs were legitimate. Queries deviating from natural, human-like phrasing were removed, and only QA pairs with short answers containing entities were retained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation process involved two stages: LLM-based annotation using GPT-4o to generate synthetic QA pairs based on gathered information, followed by human annotation to rewrite and calibrate the questions and answers for correctness and consistency. The QA pairs were categorized into single-source and multi-source types, simulating different human web-navigation behaviors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: GPT-4o for initial annotation and crowd-sourced human annotators for quality control and refinement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process ensured that the QA pairs were accurate, concise, and required multi-step reasoning. Human annotators verified the legitimacy of the queries and answers, ensuring they met strict criteria for relevance and correctness.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o, Beautiful Soup (for extracting HTML button data and markdown content from web pages)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will be available on HuggingFace Datasets. The authors mention a collection of approximately 14k silver QA pairs that can serve as supplementary training data, though these are not yet carefully human-verified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset focuses on evaluating LLMs' ability to perform web traversal and information extraction, which can have implications for improving AI systems' ability to handle complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks in real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may inherit biases from the official websites used as sources, particularly in domains like conference, organization, education, and game, where the information structure and content may reflect specific biases or priorities of those domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs, which may not fully capture the complexity of real-world web navigation tasks. The dataset does not include multimodal environments (e.g., screenshots), which could provide additional context for web traversal tasks. The benchmark focuses on text-based reasoning and does not account for visual or interactive elements of web pages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine-tuning for evaluating LLMs' web traversal and information extraction capabilities. The dataset is designed to assess the ability of LLMs to handle complex, multi-step information-seeking tasks in real-world scenarios.
